{"baseRefName":"main","body":"### Byte-preservation checker repair at `b7f45176`

The independent re-review found the valid-input inverse oracle and earlier five-site controls sound, with one P3 gap: numeric equality accepted signed-zero byte changes. Interior and already-Hermitian pass-through now use component byte comparisons, with a shared host/native checker and genuine signed-zero fixtures. General projected boundary comparisons retain their numerical contract and tolerances.

Focused host CTest 1/1 PASS; shared signed-zero controls and direct-DFT/double-FFTW oracle checks PASS; all three old-comparison mutants are rejected. [Commands and precise limits](https://github.com/KingAlejandro/MotionCorr-standalone/blob/b7f4517669b3eae2f7d83f767b1ef6c7bf3681ad/docs/post_rc0/issue253/signed-zero-review-20261022.md). Production source and the 2e-6 gates are unchanged. New native GPU execution and full native suites are UNRUN for the updated tests; historical counts below retain their exact recorded revisions. [Current-head CI](https://github.com/KingAlejandro/MotionCorr-standalone/actions/runs/39766117151) **PASS**: Linux CPU CTest 75/75 including HermitianProjectionOracle, known-motion/smoke checks and CUDA compile-only.

---

Fixes #253. Fractional shifts and CCF cropping can leave the self-conjugate half-spectrum columns invalid for C2R. One small kernel projects those columns in all five CUDA inverse consumption buffers. It preserves resident spectra and already-Hermitian pairs; the CPU path, peak fitting, metadata/publication behavior and existing tolerances are unchanged.

The review response adds test-only checks of the actual buffer immediately before every C2R. All five per-site projection-removal mutants fail the Hermitian invariant independently of undefined cuFFT behavior, including both CCF consumers. There is no added production runtime overhead. The A100 4096² numerical leak remains characterization, not a required negative-control result.

Current native validation, source `30d35d41`, 4GPUs A100 80 GB, eight CPUs, Release / CUDA 12.8.61 / cuFFT 11.3.3:

- CPU **74/74**, CUDA **115/115**, no skips. CUDA+nvCOMP **117/118**, then **1/1** for the sole source-archive/Git-metadata fixture failure after attaching the exact revision; this is not a clean 118/118 full run.
- Five raw per-site mutants exit **1** before cuFFT; their expected-invariant-failure CTest controls pass in both CUDA builds. Fixed CCF checks **1,372** inverses; the numerical matrix checks **64** production buffers.
- **112** standalone injections explain the 4096² constant/alternating-x leakage with fitted coefficients approximately −1 and residual RMS ≤2.61e−7. Other tested sizes, including 1D 4096, discard the injected incompatible component. Results are consistent with the proposed packing mechanism; cuFFT internals remain unverified.

[Current commands, source/resource identities, counts, raw archive, per-site failures and per-size injection table](https://github.com/KingAlejandro/MotionCorr-standalone/blob/af2a5900357e8e4dcdd83fb833ccb7e4fdaa5817/docs/post_rc0/issue253/review-20261021/README.md).

Earlier movie/product evidence remains source-bound to [the original record at 8b55d5da](https://github.com/KingAlejandro/MotionCorr-standalone/blob/8b55d5dae8815e4648758620750496e4acd533c5/docs/post_rc0/issue253/README.md): the 4096² production inverse maximum relative error changed **0.0121215 → 5.22079e−7**; the 10216 5×5 movie CPU/CUDA RMSE changed **0.823504 → 0.0369230 non-DW**, **0.434362 → 0.0173291 DW**. Every backend gate remained **FAIL**; S1 is not closed. Those products were not rerun in this review response.

Intentional CUDA product changes still require maintainer sign-off and independent review before merge. Broader QF replays, other devices/library versions, D14 timing and downstream science were not rerun; earlier qualification SHAs remain unchanged. No new tag or scientific-equivalence claim.
","comments":[{"id":"IC_kwDOUnH-pc8AAAABd4UGsw","author":{"login":"KingAlejandro"},"authorAssociation":"OWNER","body":"## Review of PR #254 at 8b55d5dae8815e4648758620750496e4acd533c5

The production change looks sound on inspection. I checked pair ownership/indexing, odd/even dimensions, self-conjugate bins, idempotence, normalisation, stream ordering, and all five inverse-consumption sites. Projection is applied to consumption scratch rather than repeatedly modifying resident spectra. I found no concrete production-kernel defect in this review.

The committed evidence is substantial: the raw archive hash and all 464 indexed files were verified, including JUnit totals of 74/74 CPU, 110/110 CUDA and 113/113 CUDA+nvCOMP, with no skips. The native logs show the identical-spectrum inverse error changing from 0.0121215384 on main/the no-projection mutant to 5.22078981e-7 with the fix. Current-head Linux CI is green, but its CUDA job is compile-only; these native results are committed evidence, not a new GPU rerun by this review.

### P2: make the mutation test independent of undefined cuFFT behaviour

[CMakeLists.txt lines 759–761](https://github.com/KingAlejandro/MotionCorr-standalone/blob/8b55d5dae8815e4648758620750496e4acd533c5/CMakeLists.txt#L759-L761) registers the no-projection mutant unconditionally; [the test's pass/fail logic](https://github.com/KingAlejandro/MotionCorr-standalone/blob/8b55d5dae8815e4648758620750496e4acd533c5/tests/cuda_hermitian_inverse.cpp#L138-L149) requires the malformed 4096² input to produce a numerical mismatch.

cuFFT explicitly leaves non-Hermitian C2R input behaviour undefined. A different GPU/library version/plan could discard the incompatible component and happen to match FFTW, causing this negative-control test to fail despite correct production code. This is a portability concern from the test contract, not a reproduced failure on another GPU.

Please make the mutation check deterministic by asserting the Hermitian boundary invariant immediately before C2R: conjugate pairing on x=0 and, for even width, x=Nx/2; real self-conjugate bins. Cover all five production callsites, particularly the two CCF consumers whose present cross-path checks can agree while sharing an omission. Keep the demonstrated A100 numerical leakage as a characterised regression, rather than requiring every cuFFT implementation to misbehave identically on invalid input.

### CPU applicability and scientific scope

The malformed-boundary condition is shared with CPU: fractional Fourier shifts phase the stored boundary bins, CPU CCF cropping/products reach the inverse directly, and [NewFFT invokes fftwf_execute_dft_c2r without an explicit projection](https://github.com/KingAlejandro/MotionCorr-standalone/blob/8b55d5dae8815e4648758620750496e4acd533c5/src/jaz/single_particle/new_ft.cpp#L389-L397). FFTW's documented contract also assumes Hermitian input; it does not promise generic sanitisation.

In an independent local check using single-precision FFTW 3.3.10, arbitrary half-spectra versus explicitly projected copies agreed within max-relative 1.25e-7 across nine odd/even geometries, including 4096². That supports the observed interpretation: current FFTW effectively discards the incompatible component, whereas the demonstrated cuFFT path leaks it into the real output. This patch explicitly makes CUDA follow the existing CPU result. It should not be described as “the mathematical issue cannot occur on CPU.”

This is a valid compatibility/contract repair, not proof that the shared fractional-Nyquist or crop/folding convention is scientifically optimal. For example, the existing double-Nyquist checkerboard convention under a half-pixel shift in both axes differs from separable symmetric Nyquist interpolation. That predates this PR and should be specified/tested separately, not silently changed here. Nor does this PR alone close residual trajectory divergence or establish downstream scientific equivalence.

**Recommendation:** retain the narrowly scoped production fix; strengthen the deterministic invariant/mutation coverage before treating the test as portable. Keep Nyquist/cropping policy and downstream validation as explicit follow-ups rather than broadening this patch.

References: [FFTW multidimensional transform contract](https://www.fftw.org/fftw3_doc/Multi_002ddimensional-Transforms.html), [cuFFT transform requirements](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cufft/index.html#fourier-transform-types).

Reviewed the projection helper and the five production callsite changes at `8b55d5da`, plus `tests/cuda_hermitian_inverse.cpp`. I found no additional concrete production-kernel defect: pair ownership is disjoint, odd widths do not acquire a fictitious x-Nyquist column, self-paired rows are handled, and projection happens on consumption scratch rather than repeatedly altering the resident spectra. I support keeping this a narrow contract repair, separate from #257 and from a new Nyquist-resampling convention. This is source inspection, not a fresh GPU run.

The existing deterministic-invariant request is correct. **One additional test-oracle detail:** the positive reference in `tests/cuda_hermitian_inverse.cpp` currently phases the half-spectrum and passes it directly to `fftwf_plan_dft_c2r_2d` / `fftwf_execute`, without explicitly restoring Hermitian boundary conditions. Thus the positive reference also relies on the observed behavior of an out-of-contract input, not just the no-projection mutant. FFTW's documentation describes C2R on Hermitian input; generic sanitisation is not the API contract.

Please make the revised tests distinguish three claims:

1. **Portable input invariant and callsite coverage.** In a test-only instrumented build, inspect the actual buffer immediately before each of the five production C2R calls. Assert conjugacy on x=0 and x=Nx/2 when present, real self-paired bins, and finite values for the finite fixture. Use fixtures with a demonstrated nonzero pre-projection defect. Remove each callsite projection separately and require an invariant failure *before* calling the FFT. Exercise both CCF consumers and relevant global/local/retry routes; two implementations agreeing is not coverage if they share the same omission.
2. **Defined output oracle.** Independently construct/project the host reference buffer first, then use a valid real inverse or an explicit full-complex high-precision reference. Include isolated boundary modes and legitimate complex conjugate pairs, unchanged interior bins, zero/integer/fractional shifts, odd/even dimensions, idempotence and resident-buffer immutability. Keep original-byte copies because C2R may overwrite its input. Do not generate the only oracle by reusing the production projection helper.
3. **Historical A100 characterization.** Retain the observed 4096² raw-input leak and its disappearance after repair, including device/toolkit/plan details. Do not require another supported GPU/cuFFT plan to produce that same invalid-input artifact for the suite to pass.

### Why CUDA changes while CPU is currently left alone

Both paths can create incompatible boundary values. The tested FFTW implementation effectively discards that component; the measured cuFFT path can turn it into a real-image artifact. This patch makes the CUDA input valid and selects a result close to that observed CPU behavior. That is a reason to fix CUDA now, not evidence that CPU input construction is mathematically exempt. An explicit CPU-consumption projection can be considered separately with CPU regression and cost tests. Likewise, the shared fractional-Nyquist/crop-folding policy remains a separately specified scientific choice.

Use valid-input mathematical/property tests as the acceptance basis. Exact CPU equality and lower end-to-end RMSE are useful diagnostics, not the definition of correctness. After the test update, retain the exact tested SHA and affected native suites; no merge or maintainer sign-off is implied by this comment.

Primary contracts: [cuFFT 12.8 §2.3](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/12.8.1/cufft/index.html#fourier-transform-types), [FFTW multidimensional real transforms](https://www.fftw.org/fftw3_doc/Multi_002ddimensional-Transforms.html).","submittedAt":"2026-10-21T00:05:27Z","includesCreatedEdit":false,"reactionGroups":[],"state":"COMMENTED","commit":{"oid":"8b55d5dae8815e4648758620750496e4acd533c5"}},{"id":"PRR_kwDOUnH-pc8AAAABTZa6aw","author":{"login":"KingAlejandro"},"authorAssociation":"OWNER","body":"## Updated review: input-contract coverage improved; finish the independent output oracle

Reviewed the delta `8b55d5da..af2a5900`, `tests/cuda_hermitian_check.h`, the revised registrations and `tests/cuda_hermitian_inverse.cpp`. This is source/retained-evidence review, not a new native run.

**Resolved:** the five site-specific projection-removal mutants now test the actual consumption buffer before C2R, including both CCF consumers. The checker fails on a dedicated invariant violation, not on a particular cuFFT response to malformed input. The production projection source is unchanged. The 4096² leak is correctly retained as characterization, and the 117/118 nvCOMP run plus 1/1 fixture rerun is not relabelled as a clean full-suite pass.

**Still outstanding from the previous review:** the positive numerical reference still phases `f`, copies it directly to `fftw_input`, then executes `fftwf_plan_dft_c2r_2d` without restoring boundary conjugacy (`tests/cuda_hermitian_inverse.cpp`, approximately lines 76–88 at this head). Thus the negative test is now portable, but the output oracle still relies on FFTW's observed handling of invalid input. The separate injection program's projected-input controls do not change this production-path test reference.

Please independently project the host reference before its real inverse, or use an explicitly defined full-complex high-precision inverse of a valid spectrum. Keep the unprojected FFTW result as an optional compatibility observation only. For small isolated modes, an analytic/direct-DFT oracle is stronger than a second implementation of the same helper.

Also make the positive tests discriminate **the selected projection**, not only symmetry: valid complex-conjugate boundary signal and interior bins must be preserved, self-paired bins must be real, and a mutant that zeros entire boundary columns must fail. A buffer of zeros is Hermitian too; invariant checks alone do not establish the correct operator. Retain odd/even geometry, multiple frames, idempotence, scratch-only behavior and resident-byte preservation.

**Updated acceptance principle:** accept this narrow repair because every inverse receives the specified mathematically valid representation and matches an independent valid-input oracle. Exact agreement with current CPU output is not the goal. The shared CPU input-contract issue is now #266; the fractional-Nyquist/crop-folding convention remains separately specified and tested rather than silently altered here. Do not require subpixel phase composition/energy preservation at Nyquist unless the chosen interpolation convention actually guarantees it; those are clean tests for strictly sub-Nyquist inputs.

The new injection evidence is consistent with constant and alternating-x leakage on the tested 4096² implementation. It strengthens the mechanism characterization, but inspecting cuFFT internals or proving a scientific interpolation policy is not necessary to justify fixing the input contract.
